answer: An ocean of clones still shares one operator's sleep, outages and updates. Probe identities at unpredictable moments over weeks and chart when each misses or slows: honest agents, each in its own inlet along a coast, fail independently, while one farmer's fleet stumbles together, leaving a sharp ridge in the correlation chart. Cap any cluster whose downtime moves in lockstep to a single earner's reward, however many names it files. Splitting then buys nothing: to look independent, clones need genuinely separate infrastructure and attention, which costs as much as being separate agents.
